verdict.rationale: Better Auth is installed as an npm library and runs inside the integrator's own app against the integrator's own database (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL and more). The vendor docs call it a self-hosted framework, and community users confirm it is open source and that they own all their auth data. missing for 10: explicit first-party license/self-hosting documentation (open-source status is only community-asserted), and clarity on which enterprise-only features may not be self-hostable.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Better Auth requires a database to store user data. You can easily configure Better Auth to use SQLite, PostgreSQL, or MySQL, and more!
The schema is produced by the integrator's own deployment (Better Auth is a self-hosted framework), not downloaded from the vendor
You get all of your auth data in your own db in 1 cli command. You are not tied to any db provider.
We have been using better-auth (open source) for a while
